bottleneck: Psychedelics show striking antidepressant effects lasting months from single doses, but whether the therapeutic mechanism is the subjective experience, the induced neuroplasticity, or the 5-HT2A receptor signaling itself is unresolved. If the trip is unnecessary, non-hallucinogenic analogs could treat millions without the clinical burden of supervised sessions; if the mystical experience is essential, therapy must remain intensive, expensive, and hard to scale. The field cannot optimize what it cannot separate, and trials cannot easily blind the unmistakable psychedelic state, contaminating the evidence base.
current_state: Trials continue with supervised dosing; non-hallucinogenic analogs are in development but unproven. The mechanism debate is unresolved and shapes every regulatory decision.
title: Psychedelic therapy mechanism unresolved
why_it_blocks: A breakthrough depression treatment is stuck in boutique clinics because nobody knows which part does the healing. Resolving the mechanism decides whether psychedelic therapy scales to millions or stays rarefied.
